text: One of the biggest mistakes men make in dating is living inside the woman's reality instead of their own. They adjust to her rules, her timeline, her boundaries, her idea of how things should happen. And over time, the interaction becomes completely shaped by her frame. So today, I want to talk about something that is extremely important in dating. Having your own reality, your own frame, to which you should stick. A lot of guys think dating success depends on clever lines, the right jokes, or answering a woman's questions correctly. This can be important, but it is secondary to the frame you operate from. Let me give you a situation that happens more often than you think. A guy meets a girl and starts going on a date with her. First date, second date, third date, fourth date, fifth date, and nothing happens. Maybe a kiss, maybe not even that. Sometimes this situation continues for months, sometimes even years. I've heard cases where a couple was basically together for years and still had no intimacy. So what's the problem? Usually, the problem is very simple. The girl's reality becomes the dominant frame. She says something like, I'm not ready yet. I think people should wait a long time. I think intimacy should happen only after a very serious stage. And the guy simply accepts it. Look, let me be clear. If the girl has her own standards, good for her. But if these standards go against what you want, your principles, your frame, but you still go for it just to have a chance with her, this is bad. Let me give you a descriptive analogy. You go on a date, you sit down, the waitress brings the drinks, and the girl pulls out a jar full of shit and says, in my life, I have a tradition. On the first date, I smear guys with shit. What would you say? I hope you would say something like, are you crazy? Absolutely not. Because your reality tells you that behavior like that is unacceptable. But when a girl sets smaller rules, many guys suddenly accept them. She says, no kissing for five dates. Or before anything happens, a guy should buy me expensive gifts. And the guys go, OK, maybe that's normal. If you constantly adapt to her rules, her boundaries, her worldview, something interesting happens. She might still spend time with you. She might still go on a date with you. But she stops seeing you as the man she desires. At best, you become convenient, the guy who pays for dinner, the guy who takes her to nice places. But attraction disappears. This is why boundaries matter. This is why you need to operate from your own reality in dating, your own standards. For example, if a girl behaves rudely on a date, you say something about it. If she keeps doing it, you end the date. If she disrespects you, you walk away. These are basic boundaries. You can also have boundaries around attraction and progression. For example, it could be your view that if you like a girl and a girl likes you, some physical escalation happens within the first few dates. And if a girl doesn't share that reality, that's fine. That doesn't mean you need to change yours, endlessly adapting to her frame. It simply means you see things differently and you are not compatible in the first place. So the best course of action is to be polite, thank her for her time, and walk away. So once again, guys, have your own standards, your own reality, your own frame, and stick to it. Ironically, this should make your dating life much more successful.
